assumptions.text: Intrusive: an import of a package outside the upstream's declared interface, a go:linkname into it, or an unsafe.Pointer conversion of its type. Functional: connascence of algorithm, execution, timing, value or identity spanning the pair, including clones. Model: a reference exposing an upstream type whose role is not contract. Contract: every other reference. A subsystem without a declared interface gives no intrusive evidence by import.

High strength is functional or intrusive. High distance is an ordinal of 7 or more: a module, owner or deploy boundary, or approved asynchronous integration. A subsystem boundary within one team and one binary is medium distance, 4, as DDD calls a bounded context.

Strength ordinals contract 1, model 3, functional 8, duplicated code 9, intrusive 10; volatility supporting or generic 3, core or unjudged 10; balance = max(|S−D|, 10−V)+1. archfit's ordinals and formula, not checked against the book; the score is reported, never gated.

Volatility is the upstream subsystem's subdomain from an approved verdict; an unjudged subsystem counts as core. Churn is evidence for the verdict, and supports two diagnostics: 20 or more commits on a supporting or generic subsystem, and none on a core one.
A subsystem's owner is the model's, or else the union of the owners CODEOWNERS gives its packages' files, with GitHub's last-match rule. Git authorship is never an owner.

A binary is a main package in scope and everything it imports. Two packages no binary holds together lie across a deploy boundary; only couplings without an import, such as clones or shared values, can cross one.
Shared kernel, partnership and conformist share a model on purpose; customer-supplier comes from Learning Domain-Driven Design, not coupling.dev.
A package with 10 or more importers and an intrusive, or factual functional, upstream dependency is a finding.

A subdomain slot opens for a subsystem another depends on, or for every subsystem when a revision range gives churn; a bounded-context slot opens for either end of a model-level pair. Each slot not opened is listed in skipped, with the reason.

Two subsystems co-change when at least 2 commits of the range changed both; their score is shared ÷ √(commits of each). A commit changing more than 40 files is a sweep and counts toward neither pair. A pair scoring 0.5 or more with no import either way is a hidden-coupling candidate. A hotspot is commits × summed cyclomatic complexity.

Coverage attributes each block of a go test -coverprofile profile to the function holding its first line. A package at least 3 packages import, whose tests run less than 50% of its statements, is an untested-dependency candidate.

A pair lists at most 20 pieces of evidence, with evidenceCount the total, and an upstream-exposure finding at most 20 dependents, with the total in its message. The report lists at most 20 hotspots and 20 packages of coverage, ranked; capped says when a list was cut, and candidates are drawn from the whole list.
